evidence.says: Winthrop's Ross Allan Webb papers include his book Kentucky in the Reconstruction Era.

basis: The Winthrop archive identifies the author of a work on side a, but the sources found do not establish that he wrote the 1956 thesis on side b. The shared name and compatible dates alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: Robert Edward Lee Knight wrote Industrial Relations in the San Francisco Bay Area and taught economics at Maryland from 1960 to 1994.
Robert Knight completed a PhD on British policy towards Austria in 1986 and taught at Loughborough.
Robert Knight of Loughborough edited Ethnicity, Nationalism and the European Cold War.

basis: The book author and the Loughborough historian have distinct careers, but the available sources do not establish that the latter wrote the 2008 review assigned to b. The shared name and subject alone do not settle the review author’s identity.

evidence.says: Names Emily E. Straus as author of Death of a Suburban Dream, published in 2014.

basis: The book is attributed to Emily E. Straus, but no accessible source found links its author to the 2011 review. The H-Net review page could not be accessed, so the shared name and subject do not establish identity.

evidence.says: Douglas Owen Baldwin wrote Political and Social Behaviour in Ontario, a 1973 PhD thesis at York University.
Douglas Baldwin co-edited Gaslights, Epidemics and Vagabond Cows and was a professor at Acadia University.

basis: The sources identify the dissertation author and the book editor, but do not connect the dissertation to the book author or establish a shared institutional affiliation in the relevant years. The matching name and subject are insufficient to establish identity.

evidence.says: The American Naval Revolution is by Walter R. Herrick Jr., published by Louisiana State University Press in 1966.

basis: The review identifies the book's author but does not connect him to the dissertation. The shared name and overlapping subject are insufficient to establish identity.

evidence.says: Michael Beaussenat Palmer (1946–) wrote Des petits journaux aux grandes agences and was a CNRS and Oxford researcher in 1980 and a Sorbonne Nouvelle professor.
Michael A. Palmer wrote The Quasi-War and the Creation of the American Navy, a Temple University PhD dissertation in 1981.
Michael A. Palmer wrote Stoddert's War and worked in the history department at East Carolina University.

basis: The dissertation is attributed to Michael A. Palmer, the East Carolina naval historian; the book is attributed to Michael Beaussenat Palmer, a media historian at CNRS and Oxford in 1980. Their distinct names and careers support separate identities.

evidence.says: Thomas M. Leonard of Saint Joseph College published ‘The Commissary Issue in American-Panamanian Relations 1900–1936’ in 1973.

basis: The source identifies a scholar associated with the commissary issue, but the searches did not establish who wrote America's Armed Vision or connect that thesis to him. The two thesis records alone do not establish whether the authors are the same person.

evidence.says: A 1971–1972 fellowship listing places Victoria Brown at the University of Washington researching the political integration of Transylvania into Greater Rumania.
Victoria Bissell Brown, author of The Education of Jane Addams, is listed as a Wisconsin graduate in 1972 and MA in 1974.
Victoria Bissell Brown, author of The Education of Jane Addams, has a PhD from the University of California, San Diego.

basis: The Transylvania researcher held a University of Washington fellowship in 1971–1972, while the Jane Addams author graduated from Wisconsin in 1972 and earned an MA there in 1974. These overlapping educational trajectories indicate different scholars.

evidence.says: A review of The East India Company and Religion identifies the author's 1988 London PhD thesis.
Cites Penelope Carson, Soldiers of Christ: Evangelicals and India, as a 1988 University of London PhD thesis.
Cites Penelope Carson, Russian Art in the Silver Age: The Role of 'Mir Iskusstva', as a 1974 Indiana University PhD thesis.

basis: The book author is associated with a 1988 London doctorate, while the other key represents a 1974 Indiana doctorate in a different field. These distinct doctorates support treating the keys as different people, though the sources do not explicitly compare them.

evidence.says: Christoph Jahr wrote the review of Messerschmidt's Militarismus - Vernichtungskrieg - Geschichtspolitik, published 3 January 2008.
Christoph Jahr's profile lists Gewöhnliche Soldaten and a Humboldt University Berlin position from 1997 to 2008.

basis: The review and the profile identify a Christoph Jahr, but the reviewed source does not establish the reviewer's affiliation or link the review to the books. The matching name and subject alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: The University of Nebraska repository lists The Role of Mirabeau in the French Revolution under David Manford Epstein.
The Journal of Roman Studies lists Personal Enmity in Roman Politics, 218–43 B.C. by David F. Epstein.

basis: The dissertation author is David Manford Epstein, while the book is attributed to David F. Epstein. The differing middle initials suggest a distinction, but the sources do not establish whether these names represent different people or link the works to one person.

evidence.says: German-Swedish relations, 1939-1942 is a 1976 University of Denver dissertation by John Miller West.
John G. West wrote The Politics of Revelation and Reason and Darwin Day in America and holds a Ph.D. in government from Claremont Graduate University.
John Miller West has a 1976 University of Denver Ph.D. and a 1987 University of Michigan J.D.

basis: The dissertation is by John Miller West, whose Denver doctorate and subsequent legal career differ from those of John G. West, the author of the books and a Claremont doctorate holder. The different names and documented careers strongly indicate two people.

evidence.says: The catalog credits Literatur und Justiz in der Weimarer Republik (1988) to Klaus Petersen, born 1937.
The University of Southern Denmark's 2005 report identifies Klaus Petersen as an H-Skand editor and lists work with Urban Lundberg.

basis: The catalog identifies the author on side a, and a university report identifies another Klaus Petersen connected with H-Skand and the reviewed book's author. The report does not identify the reviewer or establish that the reviewer is either scholar, so the pair cannot be resolved confidently.

evidence.says: The Scientia de ponderibus in the later Middle Ages is a 1967 University of Wisconsin doctoral thesis by Joseph Edward Brown.
Joseph Epes Brown recorded The Sacred Pipe and received a doctorate in anthropology and history of religions from the University of Stockholm.

basis: The thesis is attributed to Joseph Edward Brown, while The Sacred Pipe is associated with Joseph Epes Brown, whose doctorate was in a different field at Stockholm. The distinct full names and doctoral careers indicate two people.

evidence.says: Pamela Stewart lists Invisible Revolutions as her University of Arizona history dissertation and ASU history positions from 2002 to 2022.
Pamela J. Stewart is based in Pittsburgh anthropology and coauthored Witchcraft, Sorcery, Rumors, and Gossip in 2004.

basis: The dissertation author pursued a history career at Arizona State while the author of the other key's book pursued an overlapping anthropology career based at Pittsburgh. These are distinct careers in the same years.

evidence.says: Robert Asher was a history graduate student at the University of Minnesota in 1969.
Robert Asher taught history at Connecticut and received a Minnesota PhD in 1971 for a thesis on workmen's compensation.
The United Nations and economic and social co-operation (1957) is by Robert E. Asher, born 1910.
Robert E. Asher coauthored The World Bank since Bretton Woods with Edward S. Mason.

basis: The Minnesota history graduate student who wrote the compensation dissertation had a contemporaneous career distinct from the established author of works on international development. Their different careers and simultaneous publications support separate identities.

evidence.says: Palgrave identifies John Gibney as author of Ireland and the Popish Plot and a postdoctoral fellow at NUI Galway.
Irish History Online attributes Ireland and the Popish Plot (2009) to Gibney, John, 1976-.

basis: The publisher and catalogue identify the author of the book on side b, but the sources found do not link him to the H-Albion review on side a. Shared name and subject alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: The directory lists Andrew Craig's The Limits of Success as a completed 1983 dissertation at Bowling Green State University.
Andrew Gordon Craig's Movement for the Reformation of Manners is a 1980 University of Edinburgh PhD thesis.

basis: The records identify different history doctorates at different universities only three years apart. This strongly indicates two scholars, although the sources do not explicitly compare them.

evidence.says: Peter Knight wrote Conspiracy Culture, joined Manchester in 2000 and previously held a postdoctoral fellowship at Nottingham.
Peter G. Knight completed the history PhD dissertation MacArthur's Eyes at Ohio State University in 2006.
Peter Knight of the United States Military Academy presented Through MacArthur's Eyes on military intelligence in Korea in 2007.

basis: The dissertation author's Ohio State history doctorate and subsequent military history work at the United States Military Academy indicate a different career from the Conspiracy Culture author, who held a postdoctoral fellowship before joining Manchester in 2000. The distinction is inferred from their overlapping career histories.

evidence.says: The publisher lists Visions of Annihilation among Rory Yeomans's publications.

basis: The publisher identifies the author of the book on side a, but the permitted sources found do not directly connect that author to the review on side b. The shared name and subject are insufficient to establish identity.

evidence.says: Allen Roberts wrote the December 2008 H-AfrArts review of Exploring Visual Culture.
UCLA professor Allen F. Roberts identifies A Dance of Assassins (2013) as his monograph.

basis: The review and the UCLA profile do not establish that their authors are the same person. Their names and fields overlap, but no source found links the review to the author of the book.

evidence.says: Simon Middleton reviewed Emma Hart's Building Charleston for H-South in September 2012.
Simon Middleton wrote From Privileges to Rights, published in hardcover in 2006; the author teaches at the University of Sheffield.

basis: The review and the book have the same author name, but the review gives no affiliation and the sources found do not link the two works to one person. Shared subject matter alone is insufficient to establish identity.

evidence.says: Francisco J. Beltrán Tapia is a professor at NTNU; his publications include ‘Where are the missing girls?’ and ‘The uneven transition towards universal literacy in Spain’.
Francisco Beltrán Tapia has a doctorate in economic history from Oxford and was a Cambridge postdoctoral researcher from 2014.
Francisco X. Tapia's dissertation ‘The existence and development of the town meeting (cabildo abierto) in Spanish Colonial America’ is listed at Georgetown in 1963.

basis: The two records identify scholars with differently named doctorates and careers separated by decades: Beltrán Tapia was an Oxford-trained postdoctoral researcher from 2014, while Francisco X. Tapia wrote the Georgetown dissertation in 1963. The NTNU publication list connects Beltrán Tapia to works on side a.

evidence.says: Charles Bright wrote The Powers that Punish and was a historian at the University of Michigan.
Charles C. Bright earned a Yale doctorate in 1970 and began teaching at Michigan in 1970.

basis: The Michigan author is identifiable, but I could not independently verify the 1974 thesis or its author. The two different thesis titles alone do not establish whether they represent different people.

evidence.says: Lists The Terrace of the Great God at Abydos (1974) by William Kelly Simpson.
William Kelly Simpson completed a PhD in 1954 on the pyramid of Amenemhet I and was a Yale professor from 1965 to 2004.
Billy Simpson's 1973–1974 interviews were research for his PhD dissertation on the Loyalist Democratic Party of Mississippi.

basis: The Yale Egyptologist had completed a different PhD twenty years earlier and was a professor during the research for the Loyalist Democratic Party dissertation. The distinct doctoral projects and overlapping careers strongly indicate different scholars.

evidence.says: Joseph Jones graduated from Queen's University's history PhD program in 1980 and taught there from 1981 to 1983.
Joseph Jones wrote Politics of Transport in Twentieth-Century France, published by McGill-Queen's University Press.

basis: Queen's identifies a 1980 history PhD graduate named Joseph Jones, but the available sources do not connect the named dissertation to the book or identify the book's author with that graduate. The overlapping subject and year alone are insufficient to establish identity.

evidence.says: Roger Peace reviewed Antony Adolf's Peace: A World History in January 2010.
Roger Peace earned a doctorate at Florida State University and authored A Call to Conscience and A Just and Lasting Peace.

basis: The review identifies its author only as Roger Peace; the sources found do not connect that review to the author of the books. The shared name and subject alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: The book Early New England: A Covenanted Society is by David A. Weir and was published in 2005.
David A. Weir reviewed Ralegh's Country in The Sixteenth Century Journal in 1987.
The 2013 Church History index credits David A. Weir with the review of Politics Reformed.

basis: The sources confirm works on both sides but do not establish that their authors are the same person. The shared name and subject are insufficient to decide identity.

evidence.says: Manfred Clauss reviewed Wolfgang Reinbold's Propaganda und Mission im ältesten Christentum in H-Soz-Kult on 30 August 2001.
The library catalogue lists Mithras: Kult und Mysterien by Manfred Clauss, published by Beck in 1990.

basis: The review and book are credited to the same name, but the sources found do not establish that their authors are the same person. A shared subject alone is insufficient to merge the keys.

evidence.says: Helen Gurley Brown wrote Sex and the Single Girl and edited Cosmopolitan for 32 years.
In 2000, Dr. Helen Brown was introduced as having taught at Malaspina since 1970 and earned a UBC PhD in 1999.
Vancouver Island University's history faculty lists Helen Brown as academic emerita.

basis: The review credit identifies Helen Brown with Vancouver Island University, whose historian taught at Malaspina from 1970 and earned a UBC PhD in 1999. Helen Gurley Brown's overlapping career as Cosmopolitan editor identifies a different person.

evidence.says: The authority record lists Norman Peter Zacour's An introduction to medieval institutions and Talleyrand, the Cardinal of Perigord (1301–1364), 1960.

basis: The authority record links a's book to a 1960 Talleyrand book, but does not identify b's 1954 dissertation or state that the book grew from it. The similar titles alone do not establish the required link.

evidence.says: Robert Levy wrote Ana Pauker and completed a history PhD at UCLA in 1998.

basis: The publisher identifies the author of the book and his UCLA degree, but the evidence found does not link him to the Minnesota reviewer. The different institutional affiliations alone do not establish two people.

evidence.says: Richard Warren, a PhD student in Bern's Climate and Society group, is a creator of ClimeApp.
Richard Warren's CV lists GCSEs in 2007, A levels in 2009, and a physics master's in 2014.
Richard Warren, author of Vagrants and Citizens, holds a history doctorate from Chicago and teaches at Saint Joseph's University.

basis: The ClimeApp creator's education and doctoral career at Bern differ from those of the established Saint Joseph's historian who wrote Vagrants and Citizens. The Bern CV's 2007 school qualifications also postdate the other scholar's 1994 dissertation by thirteen years.

evidence.says: Lists William Barrett Evans's 1965 University of Washington PhD dissertation, Revolutionist Thought in the Daily Worker, 1919–1939.
Lists Ballots and Fence Rails and To Die Game under William McKee Evans, professor emeritus at California State Polytechnic University, Pomona.

basis: The dissertation author is identified as William Barrett Evans, while the author of the other side's books is William McKee Evans. These distinct full names and the two different 1965 dissertations support treating them as different scholars.

evidence.says: James Welch (1940–2003) wrote Winter in the Blood and graduated from the University of Montana.
James Welch earned a University of Montana liberal studies degree in 1964 and began a creative writing master's program in 1966.

basis: The AHA record identifies the other James Welch as the author of a completed 1963 history dissertation at Saint Louis University. That doctorate precedes the novelist's 1964 undergraduate degree and 1966 start of graduate study, strongly indicating separate people.
